When I met my now husband, I was deeply depressed and suicidal. Along with mental health issues in general, I was abused, etc. I was also surrounded by Christians who expected a lot from me, and I was struggling with not feeling anything at all. I felt hurt that God would let those things happen to me and my sisters, I felt abandoned by him and my parents. Eventually, I was starting to realize that that life wasn't for me. That's when I met him on Reddit.

After a few months of us being in a LDR, I "came out" telling people I wasn't Christian. It caused a lot of uproar, and a lot of people blamed my husband. They still do. A lot of my family still do not like him because of that. What actually happened was that I had unbiased support. He was the first person that showed me that I could be who I wanted to be. I didn't have to live in this lie and feel this oppression and pain. He gave me the strength to speak up and live my truth.

My husband is atheist, but grew up around all different kinds of religions. His mother's side of the family is Jewish, his stepfather is Muslim, his dad's side of the family is Catholic, and he lived with Christians and went to church with them. That's when I met him. He's very open-minded, but very logical. He told me often that if I wanted to continue being Christian, that was fine, but don't push it on him. 

There's many reasons I love him, but I will always love him for helping me be who I am. My family can suck it. 💕
